A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASGuard research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original three-model benchmark results, attention-head interventions, linear probes, and circuit analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds OLMo experiments, additional jailbreak evaluations, and random-head controls.

M1.justification: The three-stage procedure remains circuit-based head identification, channel-wise scaling, and preventative fine-tuning with fixed scaling vectors subsequently removed. Sections 2–3 retain the same components and objectives; application to additional attacks and models does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond tense jailbreaks to GCG adversarial suffixes and LogiBreak logical reformulations. Appendix A.2.1 adds HarmBench behaviors for GCG training/evaluation and English LogiBreak data. The original JBB-Behaviors, chat-training datasets, OR-Bench, and MMLU coverage remains.

E2.justification: Representation Engineering (RepE) becomes an evaluated comparator in the retained tense benchmark, rather than merely cited background. New Table 4 adds Random Scaling and Random PFT controls. The existing SFT, DPO, Circuit Breaker, RepBend, and head-ablation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds OLMo configurations, attack-specific training, separate out-of-domain testing, and a control applying the pipeline to 10 non-circuit heads. Appendix A.2.2 specifies a 7e-6 preventative-fine-tuning learning rate for GCG/LogiBreak versus 9e-6 for Llama tense experiments. Table 2 introduces zero-clipping of negative R-Scores. The reported judge prompt also drops its opening sentence; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's brief random-ablation comparison, v2 Appendix A.3 tests learned scaling and preventative fine-tuning on non-circuit heads and reports Temporal Head intervention controls. Section 5.3 adds cross-attack generalization testing. New OLMo probe and circuit figures extend the mechanistic analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing prompt-reformulation counts and distribution-plot reporting practices are retained; additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: All 27 original main-table rows retain their numerical values. v2 adds RepE and OLMo results, including OLMo ASGuard ASR of 9% versus 28% for its base model. New Table 2 reports ASGuard ASRs of 1% on GCG and 13% on LogiBreak; the separate out-of-domain experiment reports 1% and 15%. Table 4 adds Random Scaling/PFT ASRs of 25%/5%, with Random PFT over-refusal of 89%.

T1.justification: The circuit definitions, scaling derivation, training objectives, and numbered equations remain unchanged. However, v2 Table 2 adds an effective max(0, R) definition for negative robustness scores and uses the clipped values in Overall scores. This is a limited mathematical metric-definition change, without new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The claimed validation expands from tense-jailbreak mitigation on three models to four models and explicit mitigation of GCG and LogiBreak in the introduction's contribution list. Tense manipulation becomes an example of broader targeted-jailbreak applicability. The central circuit-guided scaling and safety–utility claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning cross-attack generalization and why circuit-selected heads outperform arbitrary-head interventions in safety–utility balance. It also explains why its unified evaluation pipeline can produce ASRs different from cited papers. The original mechanistic explanation and architecture-related limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds RepE steering settings, OLMo training configurations and refusal prompts, and attack-specific learning rates. Tables 3–4 document additional vulnerable and random head lists. A new reproducibility statement describes supplementary code and instructions; the public repository disclosure and two-H100 hardware specification already existed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gradient Cuff, Mehrbod et al.'s circuit-discovery work, and the OLMo reference, with explicit positioning against detection and single-token ablation in Appendix A.3. LogiBreak receives expanded discussion, but its underlying paper was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the section sequence remain intact. Local additions include the out-of-domain subsection, random-head appendix, and reproducibility statement, alongside terminology, acknowledgments, and conference-header edits. The revision does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The main results table expands, Figure 2 gains an OLMo panel and RepE markers, and new tables display additional attacks and random-head controls. The vulnerable-head table moves to the appendix and expands. New OLMo probe/circuit figures are added, while Figures 5–6 receive corrected model/head captions without changing their plotted data.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for both the method's design and applicability. Table 4 tests the full intervention pipeline on non-circuit heads, addressing a question v1's simple ablation comparison left open. Additional attack and transfer experiments test applicability beyond tense manipulation, supported by another model and RepE comparisons. The new attack protocols remain briefly documented and uncertainty reporting is unchanged, but the added controls and broader tests materially strengthen the empirical case.
